rationale.text: The test applies only to decorative images without a caption, and code cannot tell which images those are. The glossary defines a decorative image as one with no function and no particular information relative to the content it goes with, and the caption glossary adds that an image whose adjacent text can stand in for it may be treated as decorative. Whether an image has a caption is partly judgment too: the caption glossary covers adjacent text that informs on the image, not only figure and figcaption. So no check can fault an element as surely in scope, nor pass a page, and the entry stays at none, although each condition of the test is mechanical once an element is known to be in scope. The routes follow the wording: an empty alt with no other attribute that provides a text alternative, aria-hidden="true", or role="presentation". Technical note 3 accepts role="none" as a synonym, so it is a route too; leaving it out would report as failing an image the text accepts. The methodology asks for the absence of aria-labelledby, aria-label and title on every image, whichever route it uses, while the wording asks it only with the empty alt. The entry keeps the wording's wider reading, so that an image with aria-hidden="true" and a title is not described as failing; this is a reported doubt, and a reviewer applying the methodology would be stricter. The caption limit is an exception, from the wording and technical note 1. No axe rule is tagged for this test. The custom check custom/1-2-img-empty-alt-with-alternative reports an img that has alt="", neither aria-hidden="true" nor a role of presentation or none, and a non-blank aria-label, aria-labelledby or title. If that image is decorative and has no caption, no route holds for it. The check reads all four routes, so the link lists them, but it does not examine the caption exception, and it looks only at images with an empty alt, so its scope is partial. Its fault is evidence only: the image may be informative or captioned, and then this test does not cover it. Applicability is judgment, because the test applies only to decorative images. Needs is empty: the attributes are read on the page as loaded.
